newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec shares now a good bet--Dresdner analyst.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec shares now a good bet--Dresdner analyst.

text.p: Shares of Nomura Securities Co Ltd are now a good bet despite the announcement of stiff penalties by Japanese financial authorities against the brokerage, an analyst said on Wednesday.

"I recommend Nomura as a buy, because, in the long run, the company will remain the strongest brokerage in the Tokyo market after the ongoing deregulation," said Robert Garone, an analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson Securities.
He also said that the impact of penalties against Nomura would be limited.
The Finance Ministry on Wednesday ordered Nomura to halt its own-account stock-related dealing, including options and index trading, from August 6 to December 31.

The ministry also suspended Nomura's stock-related business at all branches from August 6 to August 12, and halted its securities trading and securities futures broking at the first corporate division at its headquarters from August 6 to December 5.
Garone said he expected Nomura's parent net profit in 1997/98 to range from 10 to 30 billion yen.
He forecast parent net profits of around 50 billion to 60 billion yen for the current year before the scandal concerning Nomura's illegal payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer surfaced in March.

Nevertheless, Garone said that Nomura's expertise in the areas of investment trusts, and stock and bond underwriting will be reflected through a rebound in the company's earnings after the current business year.

He also pointed out that clients who had halted securities trading through Nomura or excluded Nomura from an underwriting syndicate were likely to resume business with the brokerage after the punishment.
